label: LIMITED_ESSE_1: EsseLimited x: the act of being of x is limited, finite in formal perfection, in…
definition: EsseLimited x: the act of being (esse) of x is limited, finite in formal perfection, in the way ST I q.7 a.1 says form received in matter has its amplitude contracted and q.7 a.2 says a created subsistent form's esse is contracted to a determinate nature. In Lean EsseLimited is a parameter; its content is fixed only by STMT-ESSE-LIMITED-ONLY-THROUGH-RECEPTION and STMT-UNLIMITED-ESSE-IS-INFINITE. It is not quantitative finitude and not the represented RootMultiplication.HasLimitingPrinciple disjunction.
note: Stipulative label for the limitation q.7 a.1-2 speak of, indexed to a thing's esse. What would source it as a definition: a materialized passage giving an account of limitation of esse independent of reception, against which the reception premise could then be tested rather than presupposed. Examples: per q.7 a.2 and De ente c.4, the esse of an angel or of a composite substance is limited. Counterexample (per q.7 a.1): the divine esse is not limited. Distinguished from limitation of matter by form (perfective determination) and from quantitative boundedness.
